title: Adaptive verification criteria and runtime mapping for verified performance profiles
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Problem: Our current Verified Performance Profile (VPP) publishing flow assumes a single static measurement per model binary and hardware class. This causes stale profiles when model variants (quantized, fused-kernel, sequence-optimized) or runtime-level configuration differ from what customers actually run. Goal: Define an adaptive verification policy that maps published profiles to runtime variants and quantization suffixes, plus a freshness/expiry policy and canary integration so published profiles remain accurate across releases and hardware. Scope: - Define canonical runtime variant taxonomy (e.g., fp16, int8-q4_0, int8-q5, fused-kernel-v2) and labels included in published profile metadata. - Extend verification harness to run across a representative matrix of batch sizes, sequence lengths, and KV-cache behaviors. - Define profile-to-runtime mapping rules used by Smart Routing and Dedicated capacity to choose compatible fallbacks. - Add expiration/freshness metadata and automated re-verify triggers (telemetry drift, infra upgrade, model push). Out of scope: full UI redesign of the Performance Catalog (handled separately), model-family canonicalization work (follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Profile schema updated to include 'runtime_variants' array and 'freshness' timestamp
Verification harness produces per-variant latency, p95, throughput and cost estimates recorded as part of the profile artifact
Smart routing can select a compatible variant based on customer's runtime capabilities and the profile mapping rules
Automated re-verify job triggers when 1) model binary updated, 2) relevant infra upgrade detected in telemetry, or 3) drift threshold exceeded
Canary publish flow exists: new profile staged to 5% of traffic with rollback on quality/latency regressions
tasks: Finalize runtime variant taxonomy with Eng (targeted naming + compatibility matrix)
Extend verification harness to run quantized/fused kernels on CI fleet and produce per-variant metrics
Define profile freshness policy and TTL defaults (proposed 90 days) and automated re-verify triggers
Add profile metadata fields to profile registry and publishing API
Implement Smart Routing compatibility checks to prefer pinned variant when exact match isn't available
Wire canary publish pipeline and dashboard alerts for regressions (latency/cost/quality)
notes: Why adaptive verification: customers run combinations of model versions, quantizations, and hardware that we can't enumerate in a single publish. Mapping improves safety of automatic fallbacks and reduces customer surprises.
Proposed TTL 90 days chosen to balance verification cost + operational risk. Shorter TTL considered (30d) but increases re-verify cost on heavy model churn.
We must include cost-per-token delta for each variant so customers and routing policies can make cost-aware choices.

Edge case: a verified 'int8-q4_0' variant may have better p95 but worse tail latency under high-concurrency due to kernel scheduling; profiling must capture both p50/p95/p99 and throughput at 5/25/100 concurrent engines.
risks: Verification cost could increase ~3x if we run a large variant matrix for every model on every commit; need sampling and canary prioritization
False confidence: mapping rules must be conservative to avoid publishing profiles that claim compatibility where performance regresses
Telemetry lag: triggers relying on telemetry may miss fast regressions if our metric pipelines have >24h lag
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): implement schema changes and run verification for 10 high-volume open models on staging fleet
Phase 2 (canary): publish adaptive profiles for 3 models to 5% production traffic; monitor latency/cost/quality for 72h
Phase 3 (gradual): expand to 50% of catalog over 6 weeks with automated re-verify jobs throttled to control cost
Phase 4 (GA): make adaptive mapping the default for newly onboarded models and provide opt-in for legacy profiles
